questions.q: How is the great train to Johannesburg described?
choices: A white man's wonder with no engine, only an iron cage on its head taking power from metal ropes overhead
A diesel express with sleeping cars
A slow ox-drawn wagon on rails
questions.explain: The electric train draws its power from overhead 'metal ropes' via a cage — a marvel to Kumalo.

questions.q: As the train reaches the level plains, why are the place names hard for Kumalo?
choices: They are in Afrikaans, a language he had never yet heard spoken
They are written in an old script
questions.explain: 'They are in the language that was called Afrikaans, a language that he had never yet heard spoken.'

questions.q: What are the 'white flat hills in the distance' that Kumalo sees?
choices: The rock brought up out of the mines after the gold has been taken from it
questions.explain: A fellow passenger explains it is mine rock — the tailings left after the gold is extracted.

questions.q: How is the mine rock brought up from underground, according to the passenger?
choices: Wound up in a cage by a great wheel
Pushed up a ramp by machines
questions.explain: 'It is wound up by a great wheel' — and the passenger points out the spinning headgear wheel.

questions.q: When Kumalo asks a young man for help, what does the young man offer to do?
choices: Carry his bag to the church
Guide him to Sophiatown and get his bus ticket for him
Find him work in a factory
questions.explain: The young man leads him toward the buses, then offers to fetch his ticket so he won't lose his place in line.

questions.q: What happens to the pound Kumalo hands the young man?
choices: The young man disappears with it around the corner and never returns
It is refunded at the ticket office
questions.explain: Kumalo has been cheated: 'you will not see him again.' There is in fact no ticket office — tickets are bought on the bus.

questions.q: Who then helps Kumalo reach the Mission House?
choices: Mr Mafolo, a businessman and 'a good son of the Church'
questions.explain: An elderly, decently dressed Anglican — Mr Mafolo — takes him by bus and on foot to the Mission House in Sophiatown.

questions.q: Who opens the door of the Mission House to them?
choices: A young, tall man in clerical dress — Msimangu
questions.explain: Msimangu greets Kumalo: 'Mr Kumalo, I am glad to greet you. Is this your first visit to Johannesburg?'

questions.q: What does Kumalo, who does not usually smoke, do once he is safely inside the lighted room?
choices: Accepts a cigarette and 'puffed like a child at his smoke'
Asks to leave immediately for Claremont
questions.explain: Feeling welcome and secure at last, he accepts a cigarette 'though it was not his custom to smoke.'

questions.q: What is the electric advertisement sign doing that Kumalo watches, baffled, from the street?
choices: Pouring water from a bottle into a glass, then reversing, with the words 'black and white'
questions.explain: The neon sign endlessly empties and refills a bottle — 'Black and white, it says... though it is red and green. It is too much to understand.'
